prompt.value: Let X and Y be two rows in the "Scores" table. X and Y are partially matching if they are either from the same city or have the same total marks (or both). Choose the correct implementation(s) of the procedure partialMatch. It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ).

explanation.value: Partial matching is an OR: same city OR same total. Option 2 uses (A or B), and Option 3 uses (A + B >= 1), both of which are True when at least one condition holds. Option 1 uses (A and B), which requires both, so it is wrong.

prompt.value: The following pseudocode is executed using the "Library" dataset. A captures the number of Fiction books which were published between 2000 and 2010 (inclusive) and are written in a language other than English. Choose the correct code for procedure doSomething. It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ).

options.value:
Procedure doSomething(X)
B = 0
if(X.Year >= 2000 or X.Year <= 2010 and X.Genre == "Fiction" and X.Language != "English"){
B = 1
}
return B
End doSomething

Procedure doSomething(X)
B = 0
if(X.Year >= 2000 and X.Year <= 2010 and X.Genre == "Fiction" and X.Language != "English"){
B = 1
}
return B
End doSomething

explanation.value: A book qualifies only when 2000 <= Year <= 2010 AND Genre is Fiction AND Language is not English. Option 1 (nested ifs) and Option 4 (a single AND) both express this. Option 2 uses 'Year >= 2000 or Year <= 2010' (true for every year), and Option 3 has the same flawed OR on the year, so both fail to filter the year.

prompt.value: The given information represents a "Shopping Bill" and may have mistakes with respect to the sanity of data. Identify all rows with such mistakes. It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ). Shopping Bill Row no. Item Category Qty Price Cost Row 1 Cereal Packed/Food 2 220 220 Row 2 Milk Fruits/Food 1 24 24 Row 3 Cupcakes Packed/Food 1 25 25 Row 4 Chocolates Packed/Food 10 10 10 Row 5 Shirts Women/Apparel 1.5 1350 2025

options.value: Row 1
Row 2
Row 3
Row 4
Row 5

explanation.value: Row 1: Cost should be Qty × Price = 2 × 220 = 440, not 220. Row 4: Cost should be 10 × 10 = 100, not 10. Row 2: Milk is categorised as 'Fruits/Food', which is the wrong category. Row 5: Qty = 1.5 is not a valid (integer) quantity of shirts. Row 3 is fully consistent (1 × 25 = 25). [If only the Cost = Qty × Price rule is intended, the answer narrows to Rows 1 and 4.]

The pseudocode may have mistakes; identify all such mistakes (if any). It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ). 1   A = 0 2   while(Table 1 has more rows){ 3       Read the first row X in Table 1 4       C = True 5       if(X.Publisher == "Penguin"){ 6           C = True 7       } 8       if(X.Author == "Narayan"){ 9           C = False 10      } 11      if(C){ 12          A = A + 1 13      } 14      Move X to Table 2 15  }

options.value: Error in Line 4
Error in Line 9

explanation.value: We want C to be True for books published by Penguin OR written by Narayan. C must start False (Line 4 wrongly sets it True, so non-matching books are counted), and a Narayan book should set C = True (Line 9 wrongly sets it False). With Lines 4 and 9 fixed, Penguin sets C True and Narayan sets C True, giving the intended OR.

prompt.value: The following pseudocode is executed using the "Scores" dataset. At the end of the execution, A captures the lowest Chemistry marks scored by a male student from Vellore. Choose the correct code fragment(s) for the marked block. It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ).

explanation.value: A starts at 101 (above the maximum mark) for a minimum search, so we keep the smaller Chemistry mark (Chemistry < A) among male students (Gender == 'M', equivalently Gender != 'F') from Vellore. Options 2 and 4 do this; Options 1 and 3 use '>' and would find the maximum.

prompt.value: A pseudocode is executed on a dataset whose words are, in order, the words of: "Surrounded by nature, Susan often takes a stroll, savoring the soothing sounds of chirping birds. Rustlings in the trees suggest squirrels beginning their day, searching for sustenance. Surely, the beauty of a sunrise holds unparalleled magic." What will be the value of count at the end of the execution? Assume upper case and lower case are ignored during comparison of letters.

explanation.value: flag starts True and becomes False permanently at the first full stop, so only words of the first sentence are examined. The code counts words starting with 'so' there: 'soothing' and 'sounds' — so count = 2.
